item.title: Lael Neale brings 1980's omnichord back to life on new album, 'As Killers Do'
item.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Lael Neale about her new album, As Killers Do. The record features mostly forgotten music-making techniques such as 8 track recording and a 1980s instrument.

item.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Ian Coss, host of the The Big Dig Season 4: Mitt & Ted, a healthcare story, about how political foes joined together to pass landmark health care legislation.

item.description: After two weeks of negotiations, international climate talks fail to reach an agreement. NPR's Rachel Waldholz was in Turkey for the conference.

item.title: Ukraine war spilling into NATO territory
item.description: The war between Russia and Ukraine once again creeps onto European territory – from attacks on ships to missiles in Poland and fresh allegations of Russian operations inside Denmark.

item.title: Rising costs leave consumers looking for Thanksgiving bargains
item.description: It's Thanksgiving week and you may have seen that turkey and gravy are more expensive. NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, about why costs are up.

item.title: Luxury development planned on land some Albanians say is theirs, not Jared Kushner's
item.description: A company working for President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner purchased 300 acres of Albanian land for more than $130 million in April. But Albanians in the area tell NPR this is not Kushner's land -- it's theirs.

item.title: What's next after a brutal stock plunge we might have seen coming
item.description: Stocks tanked this week as investors grew wary of tech investments that have seen years of growth. NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Katie Martin of the Financial Times about the global ripple effects.
